dod_intent_evidence: SDA PWSA SBIR award (Sept 2025), Army PMO UAS Blue UAS assessor contract (Mar 2026), DIU hybrid space network project with Amazon/Microsoft, and a 2023 USSF Enterprise Ground Services Phase II SBIR ($1.23M) — News + SBIR abstract sections.
score_evidence: "Programmable policy management adaptable to any CONOP or operational workflow" and "connected across contested, disrupted, or third-party networks" and "even with the typical constraints on size, weight, and power" → explicit CONOPS/DDIL/SWaP-C fluency, driving deployment_awareness_absence to near zero per the 'fluent = low score, still a keep' calibration rule

blind_spots.blind_spot: SpiderOak positions itself entirely as a component vendor selling through 'system providers' (integrators/primes) rather than owning the end-user relationship.
blind_spots.operator_reality: "Operators loving it is not adoption" — SpiderOak's own materials show they've architected themselves as a sell-through security layer, with no visible advocacy-chain narrative for how OrbitSecure survives if a prime partner's priorities shift or the integration gets deprioritized.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Zero-trust security is inherently a component/embedded technology, so the company's go-to-market naturally routes through system integrators rather than direct operator relationships.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: With SpiderOak, system providers can extend access control and data protection to edge devices, applications, and platforms—such as satellites, payloads, autonomous vehicles, or tactical radios.

blind_spots.blind_spot: On-orbit demonstrations (Ball Aerospace payload, ISS with Axiom/AWS) are framed as proof of technical feasibility, with no public mention of key/certificate rotation, revocation, or patch cadence once the asset is physically unreachable.
blind_spots.operator_reality: "Achievable" in a single on-orbit demo doesn't address the sustainment question that actually matters for a fielded space asset: how do you rotate crypto material or patch firmware on something you can never touch again?
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Public materials are written to showcase flight heritage as a sales proof point; sustainment/lifecycle mechanics are typically a later-stage engineering discussion not surfaced in marketing.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: SpiderOak's OrbitSecure technology was successfully deployed and integrated on-orbit, demonstrating that data-level zero-trust is achievable in space, even with the typical constraints on size, weight, and power.

blind_spots.blind_spot: SBIR abstract describes brokering command and control across 'US Government, Allied, and/or commercial infrastructure' with no ITAR/export-control or CMMC language anywhere in public materials.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Multi-party data brokering across US/Allied/commercial boundaries is exactly the scenario that triggers ITAR and foreign-disclosure review — the company's own compliance posture supporting that claim isn't described publicly.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Compliance posture likely exists internally for a company this far along in government contracting, but isn't surfaced as a public trust signal.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: This will enable an enterprise command brokering system that enables use of US Government, Allied, and/or commercial infrastructure for command and control.

opener_hook: SpiderOak's OrbitSecure has flown on an ISS demo and a Ball Aerospace on-orbit payload — its own materials never say who rotates keys once the asset is unreachable.
what_they_do: Zero-trust cybersecurity software for tactical-edge and space systems — demonstrated on ISS and an on-orbit payload, now contracted by SDA (PWSA) and Army PMO UAS.
